primary_sources: Pazos M, Traverso CE, Viswanathan A; European Glaucoma Society. Terminology and guidelines for glaucoma, 6th edition. Br J Ophthalmol 2025;109(Suppl 1):1-212
Gedde SJ, Vinod K, Wright MM, et al. Primary open-angle glaucoma preferred practice pattern. Ophthalmology 2021;128(1S):P71-P150
Mwanza JC, Budenz DL. Optical coherence tomography platforms and parameters for glaucoma diagnosis and progression. Curr Opin Ophthalmol 2018;29(2):101-110
Leung CK, Cheung CY, Weinreb RN, et al. Retinal nerve fiber layer imaging with spectral-domain OCT: a variability and diagnostic performance study. Ophthalmology 2009;116(7):1257-1263

rules.name: Data sufficiency check (cascade gate 1)
rules.specification: First gate of the hierarchical classification cascade: verifies measurement count and RNFL plausibility before slope analysis is attempted
rules.implementation_note: If insufficient or implausible: returns 'unclassifiable' with explicit cause. This gate prevents downstream analysis on data that cannot meaningfully support a trend.

rules.name: Floor effect detection (cascade gate 2A)
rules.specification: Detects when global RNFL has reached the measurement floor where further thinning cannot be reliably distinguished from noise
rules.implementation_note: When global RNFL is at or near the floor, slope analysis becomes unreliable. The result returns 'floor_effect' as classification with explicit caveat. This is the canonical 'structural ceiling' problem in advanced glaucoma.

rules.name: Artifact and reliability concern (cascade gate 2B)
rules.specification: Detects scan artifacts and reliability concerns that could falsely simulate progression or stability

thresholds.artifact_drop_threshold: >=4 microns drop with poor reliability indices
thresholds.segmentation_concern: Manual review flag from clinician input

rules.implementation_note: Returns 'suspicious_trend' classification with caveat. Distinct from genuine progression, which is identified at gate 5.

rules.name: RNFL slope OLS estimation (cascade gate 3)
rules.source: Standard practice for OCT trend analysis (Mwanza & Budenz 2018, Leung et al. 2009)
rules.specification: Estimates the slope of global RNFL thickness over time using ordinary least squares linear regression
rules.implementation_note: Uses global RNFL only. Sector-level and GCC analysis are not included in v1.0.

rules.name: Stable slope check (cascade gate 4)
rules.specification: Identifies stable trends where slope falls within the age-related thinning range
rules.implementation_note: Above this threshold, the trend is considered stable. Below, the cascade proceeds to gate 5 for further classification.

rules.name: Slope classification (cascade gate 5)
rules.specification: Classifies slopes that exceed the stable range into specific progression categories
rules.implementation_note: Three-tier classification at this gate. Combined with the floor effect, artifact, and signal-limited variants, M4 produces seven possible classification states total.

rules.name: Myopia-limited signal modifier
rules.specification: Modifies the M4 classification when high myopia is documented, reflecting the reduced reliability of RNFL trend analysis in high myopic eyes

thresholds.high_myopia: Spherical equivalent < -6 diopters or axial length > 26.5 mm

rules.implementation_note: Reflects the clinical principle that progression detection by RNFL is unreliable in high myopia. The result is flagged as signal-limited rather than classified as progression.

rules.name: ERM-limited signal modifier
rules.specification: Modifies the M4 classification when epiretinal membrane (ERM) is documented, reflecting structural distortion that confounds RNFL measurement
rules.implementation_note: Reflects the clinical principle that ERM-induced traction can confound RNFL trend analysis. The result is flagged as signal-limited.
